_comment: Template for the game server's config. Copy to server.json next to Server.Loader.exe
That directory is gitignored, so the real config never reaches the repo. Nothing in
here is secret by itself: the bot token lives in a separate file this only points at,
and the admin password comes from the environment (see StartServer.bat).
Every field has a default in code/server/native/Config.h, so an older config keeps
working when new fields are added - you only need the ones you want to change.
Name: Your server name
_comment_players: Raise this before inviting people. It was 4 for a while, which was exactly the size of the group.
_comment_public: Public servers announce themselves to the master list. A private one is reachable only by address - over Tailscale, in our case.
_comment_rates: TickRate is the server's simulation loop. UpdateRate is position updates per second,
per player, and is the ceiling on how smooth anyone else can possibly look - the
client's interpolation delay is derived from it too (50ms + 1500/rate), so a low rate
costs both smoothness AND responsiveness. It was 10 and looked like teleporting.

_comment: Identity and permissions come from Discord, not from anything the client claims.
With Enabled false, anyone who can reach the port can join as a plain player.
Discord._comment_guild: Developer Mode on, right-click your server, Copy Server ID.
Discord._comment_membership: Reject anyone not in the guild. Off means a valid Discord account is enough.
_comment_owner: The one account that always has full access regardless of roles. Set it to your own
Discord user id: it is the way back in if the role setup is ever broken, and it
cannot be removed by someone editing roles in Discord.
_comment_roles: Role -> permission level. Keys may be a role NAME or a role id; names are resolved
against the guild's real role list using the bot token.
Leave this empty and sensible defaults still apply: roles named dev, admin,
moderator, mod, staff and so on map to the obvious levels. Anything here overrides
those. Levels are owner, admin, moderator.
_comment_bottoken: Path to the file holding the bot token - see tools/.discord-bot.example. Needed only
to resolve role NAMES; role ids work without it. The token is never stored in this
file. NCO_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN in the environment wins if set.
_comment_rolesfile: Where to write the resolved role -> level map, so the launcher can grant the same
people the same controls the game does. Point it at your checkout's publish/roles.json
and Ship publishes it with the release. Contains ids, names and levels - no secrets.

Flecs._comment: The ECS REST API, for inspecting the live world. Keep it on localhost.
